erroriFattuali: EDSAC notation: the text gave `A25F`, with F marking a short word, as the form used in May 1949. Under Initial Orders 1 an order ended in S (short) or L (long); F came only with Initial Orders 2. Fixed: `A 25 S` with S/L explained, and the switch to F moved to the paragraph on the second version (the form used in the «Ciao, mondo»).

Initial Orders 2: «la tredicesima cella da qui» described an address counted from the current instruction. The θ/@ addresses of Initial Orders 2 count from the start of the routine (the base set by GK). Fixed: «dall'inizio di questo pezzo».
Table: «i primi BASIC» listed as interpreter examples, but Dartmouth BASIC (1964) was a compiler. Replaced with «i BASIC degli home computer».

EDSAC library: «si univano al proprio nastro» was wrong. The library tapes were copied onto the user's tape and the master copies went back to the cabinet. Fixed; added the small steel cabinet and that the library grew past 100 subroutines (Clemson, CACM).
Wheeler jump: the return was not «un salto all'indietro» but a jump back to just after the calling point, and it took the subroutine's first two orders, not one. Fixed.

A-2: the text said Hopper personally handed out the code and that customers sent back fixes. The source only says Remington Rand gave customers the source code and invited them to send improvements back. Softened in the text and in the 1953 milestone.
1950 milestone «Short Code gira sull'UNIVAC I»: the UNIVAC I was accepted only in March 1951. Rewritten as «William Schmitt porta Short Code sull'UNIVAC I».

Kathleen Booth: the 1944 degree year could not be verified (sources disagree on her dates). Replaced with Royal Holloway plus her 1946 start at Birkbeck (Centre for Computing History). «Gli storici discutono» was based on Hackaday, not on historians; now «Non è chiaro».

Priority claims softened: «Nacque così la subroutine» is now «diventò uno strumento di tutti i giorni». «il primo manuale di programmazione» (in 3 places) is now «considerato il primo libro sulla programmazione». Wheeler's «primo dottorato in informatica» is now «spesso indicato come il primo»: sources say first in the UK, first of the lab, or a PhD in mathematics.
A-0: «nel 1952 creò» is now «tra il 1951 e il 1952 scrisse», matching the sources.
Source URL albert.ias.edu/20.500.12111/7941 is not a valid repository path. Replaced with the canonical handle https://hdl.handle.net/20.500.12111/7941.
correzioni: Intro: «In meno di dieci anni» changed to «Nel giro di pochi anni», so it no longer repeats the opening of chapter 5's intro.
Programmare in numeri: added a checked detail: at Manchester a 20-bit instruction was written as 4 base-32 characters (Computer 50, University of Manchester).

Booth: added what the preface of Coding for A.R.C. says (the same set of orders was meant for a future electronic machine, so relay programs could move over). This links the story to hardware. Replaced the vague «progettò il modo di programmare» with the 1958 book *Programming for an Automatic Digital Calculator*, one of very few written by a woman. Death now reads «È morta nel 2022, a cent'anni».
EDSAC: «cablate in» changed to «cablate su selettori telefonici». Added a short note that the final S has nothing to do with the opening S (subtract).
Figure caption nastro-edsac: «pronti da unire» changed to «pronti da ricopiare sul nastro di un nuovo programma».

Subroutines: library paragraph rewritten (steel cabinet, more than a hundred pieces, copying, originals returned). WWG book now «considerato il primo libro sulla programmazione»; dropped the hype «nei laboratori di mezzo mondo».
Lab block: «▶ Esegui» changed to «Esegui», and «la sfida in fondo» to «la sfida «Traduci a mano»», matching the names planned in js/lab/assemblatore.js.
Autocode: added Glennie's employer (the British armament research centre at Fort Halstead, per Knuth/HOPL) and split the long sentence. Brooker's Autocode now «disponibile dal 1954».

Hopper: «la figura chiave» changed to «una figura chiave»; removed the scrisse/scriveva repetition («preparava un elenco di richiami»); A-2 now linked to {{software libero}} as a comparison («un'idea che ricorda…»).

Dove finiscono quei bit: explained that with an interpreter the binary words that run are the interpreter's own; the codes 011/110 now say they belong to the toy CPU; «fatto al contrario» changed to «il seguito del viaggio».

Ciao note: «O13@ è la cella 64 + 13» changed to «in O13@ l'indirizzo vale 64 + 13»; EZPF described as the last line that starts the program. The teleprinter lag of the O order (it prints the character set up by the previous one) was confirmed and kept.
Protagonists: Glennie's role (Fort Halstead), Gill («primo libro sulla programmazione»), Wheeler (PhD hedged). Milestones: 1950, 1951 (×2), 1953, 1954 rewritten.

Sources: 5 checked sources added (Centre for Computing History on Booth; Smotherman/Clemson on the EDSAC; Manchester Computer 50 «The Base-32 Code»; T. Thomas on the Manchester Autocodes; Hopper, «The Education of a Computer», 1952, pp. 243–249, without URL). Confirmed that 9 of the existing sources exist (archive.org programsforelect00wilk, Wikiquote, cl.cam.ac.uk orders.notes, EDSAC99 statistics and charcodes, Hackaday, CHM profile, CACM blog, HOPL 2671 = Brief Code). Fixed the IAS URL.

Attributing «hesitating at the angles of stairs» to T. S. Eliot rests only on Wikiquote (which names Murder in the Cathedral). I kept the generic «di T. S. Eliot».

Not rechecked online, but well-established and consistent with chapter 3: EDSAC on 6 May 1949, Hopper at Eckert–Mauchly from 1949, the ~30 cm nanosecond wire, EDSAC had no division order, Wilkes's Turing Award in 1967, UNIVAC I in 1951.
